title: Squarefree group order forces every Sylow subgroup cyclic of prime order
description: Answers the parent entry's closing open question verbatim: how sharp is the Sylow nontriviality boundary in the non-prime-power direction? When |G| is squarefree the entire Sylow structure collapses to the simplest possible shape. Squarefreeness forces the p-adic valuation v_p(|G|) = 1 for every prime p ∣ |G| (factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree_dvd, via Nat.factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree). Composing this with the parent's Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity (|P| = p^(v_p|G|)) gives that every Sylow p-subgroup has order exactly p (sylow_card_eq_prime_of_squarefree), hence is cyclic of prime order (sylow_isCyclic_of_squarefree_dvd, via isCyclic_of_prime_card) — the literal statement the open question requested. The boundary becomes razor sharp: a Sylow p-subgroup has order 1 (when p ∤ |G|) or p (when p ∣ |G|), never a higher power (sylow_card_eq_one_or_prime_of_squarefree), and EVERY Sylow subgroup is cyclic with no hypothesis on p (sylow_isCyclic_of_squarefree — trivial ones cyclic by isCyclic_of_subsingleton). Specializing to S₃ (|S₃| = 6, squarefree) recovers the parent's concrete numbers as instances of the general theorem: the Sylow 2-subgroup is cyclic of order 2, the Sylow 3-subgroup cyclic of order 3. Genuinely 0-axiom.

overview.historicalContext: Sylow's first theorem gives a subgroup whose order is the full p-part of |G|, but in general that p-part can be a high power of p, and the Sylow subgroup can be large and non-abelian. The simplest possible case is the opposite extreme: when |G| is squarefree, no prime divides |G| more than once, so every p-part is just p itself. Groups of squarefree order are classical — they are exactly the Z-groups (all Sylow subgroups cyclic) with squarefree order, and Hölder (1895) classified them as metacyclic semidirect products of cyclic groups. The first structural fact underlying that classification is the one formalized here: in a squarefree-order group every Sylow subgroup is cyclic of prime order. The parent entry (CauchyGroupTheoremOQ01OQ02) built the Cauchy-to-Sylow tower and pinned down the order-2 and order-3 Sylow subgroups of S₃; its closing open question asked for exactly this general statement.
overview.problemStatement: Show that if |G| is squarefree then every Sylow subgroup of G is cyclic of prime order, recovering the parent entry's concrete S₃ picture (order-2 and order-3 Sylow subgroups) as a special case of a uniform theorem. Make the nontriviality boundary of the parent razor sharp: pin the order of every Sylow p-subgroup to be 1 or p.
overview.proofStrategy: The argument is a clean two-step composition over Mathlib's Sylow API. First, squarefreeness collapses multiplicities: Nat.factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree gives v_p(|G|) = 1 for every prime p ∣ |G|. Second, the parent's Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity computes |P| = p^(v_p|G|) for any Sylow p-subgroup P; substituting v_p = 1 and pow_one yields |P| = p. A group of prime order is cyclic (isCyclic_of_prime_card), giving cyclic-of-prime-order. For the hypothesis-free version, a case split on p ∣ |G| handles the trivial primes: when p ∤ |G|, Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_dvd gives v_p = 0, so |P| = p^0 = 1, P is a subsingleton, and isCyclic_of_subsingleton applies. The S₃ witnesses instantiate the general theorem at p = 2, 3 after proving Squarefree 6 = Squarefree (2·3) via Nat.squarefree_mul_iff and Prime.squarefree of 2 and 3.
keyInsights: Squarefreeness is exactly the hypothesis that turns Sylow's existence theorem into an exact order computation: v_p(|G|) ∈ {0,1} for all p, so |P| = p^(v_p|G|) is forced to be 1 or p — there is no room for a larger p-power.

The parent's Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity is the right lever: it states |P| = p^(v_p|G|) as an equality, so the single number-theoretic fact v_p|G| = 1 (squarefree) immediately delivers |P| = p without any further group theory.

Cyclic-of-prime-order is automatic once the order is p: a group of prime order has no proper nontrivial subgroups, hence is generated by any nonidentity element (isCyclic_of_prime_card). Squarefreeness is the only nontrivial input.

The hypothesis-free 'every Sylow subgroup is cyclic' needs the trivial primes too: when p ∤ |G| the Sylow subgroup is trivial, and triviality is cyclic via isCyclic_of_subsingleton — so the dichotomy 'order 1 or p' upgrades cleanly to 'always cyclic'.

The parent's S₃ numbers (order-2 and order-3 Sylow subgroups) are not separate computations but instances of the uniform theorem applied to the squarefree number 6 = 2·3 — exactly the 'recovering this entry's S₃ picture in general' the open question asked for.

sections.title: The Multiplicity Collapse
sections.summary: factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree_dvd: for |G| squarefree and a prime p ∣ |G|, the p-adic valuation v_p(|G|) = 1. This is the single number-theoretic engine — no prime can appear above the first power in a squarefree number.
sections.mathContext: Squarefree n and p ∣ n ⟹ n.factorization p = 1; the input that forces Sylow subgroups down to prime order.

sections.title: Every Sylow Subgroup Cyclic of Prime Order

conclusion.summary: When |G| is squarefree, the Sylow structure collapses completely: every Sylow p-subgroup has order 1 or p, and the nontrivial ones (p ∣ |G|) are cyclic of prime order. The proof is a two-step composition — squarefreeness forces v_p(|G|) = 1 (Nat.factorization_eq_one_of_squarefree), and the parent's Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity then gives |P| = p, which is cyclic (isCyclic_of_prime_card). A case split adds the trivial primes (isCyclic_of_subsingleton), so every Sylow subgroup is cyclic. Specializing to S₃ (order 6) recovers the parent's order-2 and order-3 Sylow subgroups as instances of the general theorem. Genuinely 0-axiom.
implications: Answers the parent entry's closing open question verbatim: |G| squarefree forces every Sylow subgroup to be cyclic of prime order, with the S₃ picture recovered as a special case.
Supplies the first structural fact in the classification of squarefree-order groups (the Z-group/metacyclic picture of Hölder) as a packaged, machine-checked corollary Mathlib does not record.

Demonstrates that the parent's exact order computation Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity, combined with a single squarefree-factorization fact, mechanizes the whole 'squarefree ⟹ cyclic Sylow' step with no bespoke group theory.
openQuestions: Can the full Hölder classification be packaged next — that a squarefree-order group is a semidirect product of cyclic groups, i.e. metacyclic and supersolvable — building on every-Sylow-cyclic proved here?
Does the converse-flavoured statement hold in a clean formalized form: if every Sylow subgroup of G is cyclic of prime order then |G| is squarefree, completing an iff with this entry?

crossReferences.description: Answers this parent's third open question. The parent built the Sylow tower and proved Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity-based order facts plus the nontriviality boundary; this entry sharpens that boundary under squarefreeness, forcing every Sylow subgroup to order 1 or p and recovering the parent's S₃ Sylow subgroups (orders 2 and 3) as instances of a uniform theorem.

The root Cauchy entry of the arc: Cauchy produces a subgroup of order p whenever p ∣ |G|; under squarefreeness that order-p subgroup is the full Sylow p-subgroup, so Cauchy and Sylow coincide for every prime.

mathlibDependencies.description: The order of a Sylow p-subgroup equals p ^ (Nat.factorization (Nat.card G) p); the lever that turns the squarefree valuation v_p = 1 into |P| = p.
Squarefree n, p prime, p ∣ n ⟹ n.factorization p = 1; the number-theoretic engine collapsing the multiplicity to one.
A finite group whose cardinality is a prime p is cyclic; upgrades order-p to cyclic-of-prime-order.
A subsingleton group is cyclic; handles the trivial Sylow subgroups (p ∤ |G|) in the hypothesis-free cyclicity statement.
¬ p ∣ n ⟹ n.factorization p = 0; gives |P| = p^0 = 1 for primes not dividing |G| in the dichotomy.
Squarefree (m*n) ↔ m.Coprime n ∧ Squarefree m ∧ Squarefree n; proves Squarefree 6 = Squarefree (2·3) for the S₃ witnesses.
Nat.card α = 1 ↔ Subsingleton α ∧ Nonempty α; extracts the subsingleton needed for the trivial-Sylow cyclicity case.
